results.name: shared_digit_yes_rate_diff
results.description: Among targets not in the set, yes-rate for targets sharing their last digit with some example minus yes-rate for those sharing no last digit; observed > null means people use surface digit similarity more than the model's rule/range concepts capture.
results.code:
# name: shared_digit_yes_rate_diff
# description: Among targets not in the set, yes-rate for targets sharing their last digit with some example minus yes-rate for those sharing no last digit; observed > null means people use surface digit similarity more than the model's rule/range concepts capture.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    sv = sets.values
    share = np.zeros(len(t), bool)
    inset = np.zeros(len(t), bool)
    for s in sets.unique():
        xs = np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")])
        idx = np.where(sv == s)[0]
        tt = t[idx]
        share[idx] = np.isin(tt % 10, xs % 10)
        inset[idx] = np.isin(tt, xs)
    a = share & ~inset
    b = ~share & ~inset
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: target_in_set_echo_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for trials whose target is itself one of the shown examples (should be ~1 under the model); observed < null means people reject shown examples more than the model allows (lapse/noise missing).

results.name: trial_index_slope
results.description: OLS slope of yes-response on trial_index scaled per 100 trials; nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means the model (which has no time dependence) misses drift in yes-bias over the session (positive = more yes later).

results.name: inside_minus_outside_span_same_parity
results.description: For all-even or all-odd sets, yes-rate on same-parity targets inside [min,max] of the examples minus yes-rate on same-parity targets outside it; observed > null means people show a stronger range restriction than the model, observed < null a weaker one.
results.code:
# name: inside_minus_outside_span_same_parity
# description: For all-even or all-odd sets, yes-rate on same-parity targets inside [min,max] of the examples minus yes-rate on same-parity targets outside it; observed > null means people show a stronger range restriction than the model, observed < null a weaker one.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = sets.unique()
    info = {}
    for s in u:
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        par = set(x % 2 for x in xs)
        info[s] = (min(xs), max(xs), par.pop() if len(par) == 1 else -1)
    lo = sets.map({k: v[0] for k, v in info.items()}).values
    hi = sets.map({k: v[1] for k, v in info.items()}).values
    pa = sets.map({k: v[2] for k, v in info.items()}).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    same = (pa >= 0) & (t % 2 == pa)
    ins = same & (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    out = same & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    if ins.sum() == 0 or out.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[ins].mean() - r[out].mean())

results.name: small_vs_large_set_yes_rate_diff
results.description: Overall yes-rate on sets with 1-2 examples minus yes-rate on sets with 3-4 examples; observed > null means people generalize more broadly from few examples (weaker size principle) than the model, observed < null the reverse.

results.name: distance_to_nearest_example_correlation
results.description: Pearson correlation between yes-response and the absolute distance from the target to its nearest example (excluding targets in the set); observed more negative than null means people show a steeper numeric-proximity gradient than the model.
results.code:
# name: distance_to_nearest_example_correlation
# description: Pearson correlation between yes-response and the absolute distance from the target to its nearest example (excluding targets in the set); observed more negative than null means people show a steeper numeric-proximity gradient than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    u = sets.unique()
    arr = {s: np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")]) for s in u}
    d = np.empty(len(t))
    sv = sets.values
    for s in u:
        idx = np.where(sv == s)[0]
        d[idx] = np.abs(t[idx][:, None] - arr[s][None, :]).min(axis=1)
    m = d > 0
    if m.sum() < 3 or np.std(d[m]) == 0 or np.std(r[m]) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(d[m], r[m])[0, 1])

results.name: extreme_cell_fraction
results.description: Fraction of (set,target) cells whose mean yes-rate is <=0.15 or >=0.85; observed < null means human responses are less categorical (more graded/noisy) than the model predicts, observed > null means more consensus than the model.

results.name: odd_target_after_all_even_set_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for odd targets when every example in the set is even; observed > null means the model under-produces cross-parity (similarity/noise) generalization, observed < null means it over-produces it.
